questions.q: What are the three core components of 'setting' in a prose narrative, and which component is most emphasized in the opening paragraph of "dkys es?kk ikuh ns"?
questions.a: The three core components are time (temporal), place (geographical), and social environment (socio-cultural). In the opening paragraph, the geographical component (the parched village, the scorching sun, the distant well) is most emphasized through intense sensory imagery. A wrong answer that lists only 'time and place' reveals the student ignores the social environment, which is critical in this story because the drought's impact is mediated by caste and class hierarchy. A wrong answer that picks 'time' shows the student misses the spatial and sensory dominance of the physical landscape.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the author uses the nickname "बंज लसुक" to establish both setting and atmosphere simultaneously.
questions.a: The nickname "बंज लसुक" (given because the children constantly beg for water) establishes the setting by revealing the socio-economic reality: water is so scarce that begging for it becomes a defining identity for poor children. It establishes atmosphere by conveying the dehumanizing effect of poverty — the children are reduced to their need, and the community's indifference is normalized. A wrong answer that says "it shows they are poor" only identifies setting but misses the atmospheric tone of humiliation and resignation. A wrong answer focusing only on the literal meaning of the words misses the irony that the nickname is given by those who have water but refuse to share.

questions.q: Analyze how the contrast between the landlord's household (thth) and the poor families' experience of the same drought creates a layered atmosphere. Use two specific textual contrasts.
questions.a: Contrast 1: Water access — thth has "ckYVh Hkj oQj ikuh" (full tanks of water) while the poor have "vkèkh jkr dks Hkh ekuks [kkSyrk gqvk ikuh" (water so scarce even a drop for medicine is unavailable). This creates an atmosphere of stark injustice. Contrast 2: Response to thirst — thth's children get "gkFk ls vyx f[kldk" (special food) when they refuse to eat, while the poor children are silenced with rags. This creates an atmosphere of moral corruption where privilege breeds entitlement. A wrong answer that only describes one side (e.g., "the poor suffer") fails to analyze the contrast as a structural device. A wrong answer that calls it "irony" without explaining the atmospheric shift from pity to outrage misses the analytical depth.

questions.q: Create a 4-line paragraph describing a new scene in the same village that maintains the established atmosphere but shifts the setting to nighttime. Use at least two sensory details.
questions.a: Example: "The moon bleached the empty well white, but no bucket descended. A dog licked a dry tap, its tongue clicking like a clock with no time left. Somewhere, a mother stirred waterless gruel, the spoon scraping the pot — a sound sharper than hunger." This maintains the atmosphere of desperate scarcity through auditory (clicking, scraping) and visual (bleached well) details, while shifting setting to night. A poor answer would describe a peaceful night or introduce hope, breaking the atmosphere. A poor answer using only visual details fails the sensory requirement.
